content.title: After creating a submission in the same browser session, the My Submissions count matches the submissions list
content.intent: Prove that the shared header reflects the current browser session's submission total after a real submission is created.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: equivalence partitioning + state / flow. I used the representative state transition from no known submission to one newly created submission in the same browser session because the source only grounds that the header count matches the current session's stored submissions. No covering array was needed because there is no independent multi-input interaction to combine for this journey; the risk-judged default strength would be 2 (no money/auth/data-loss factors apply).
